~~~python~~~
import pandas as pd

# Create the dataframe from the provided table
data = {
    'call sign': ['w230av', 'w269ax', 'w273ae', 'w282ae', 'w290ag'],
    'frequency mhz': ['93.9 fm', '101.7 fm', '102.5 fm', '104.3 fm', '105.9 fm'],
    'city of license': ['gadsden , alabama', 'anniston , alabama', 'albany , georgia', 'macon , georgia', 'griffin , georgia'],
    'erp w': [10, 10, 55, 27, 27],
    'class': ['d', 'd', 'd', 'd', 'd'],
    'fcc info': ['fcc', 'fcc', 'fcc', 'fcc', 'fcc']
}
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Extract the rows for w290ag and w282ae
w290ag_row = df[df['call sign'] == 'w290ag']
w282ae_row = df[df['call sign'] == 'w282ae']

# Check conditions:
# 1. Both have erp w = 27
# 2. Both have class = 'd'
# 3. w290ag has city of license = 'griffin , georgia'
# 4. w282ae has city of license = 'macon , georgia'
condition1 = (w290ag_row['erp w'].iloc[0] == 27) and (w282ae_row['erp w'].iloc[0] == 27)
condition2 = (w290ag_row['class'].iloc[0] == 'd') and (w282ae_row['class'].iloc[0] == 'd')
condition3 = w290ag_row['city of license'].iloc[0] == 'griffin , georgia'
condition4 = w282ae_row['city of license'].iloc[0] == 'macon , georgia'

answer = condition1 and condition2 and condition3 and condition4
